record.original_question: Let N be a compact closed Riemannian manifold, isometrically embedded in R^m, and let u belong to W^{1,n}(B^n, N). If u is weakly n-harmonic, meaning that it is a critical point of the n-Dirichlet energy among range variations, must u always be continuous on B^n?

evidence.quote: Despite several results that we describe in the next section, the following problem is still open. Problem 2.2 (p = n). Are all weakly n-harmonic maps u ∈ W1,n(Bn, N ) continuous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$, and let $B^n \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ denote the open unit ball. Let $N$ be a smooth, compact, closed Riemannian manifold isometrically embedded into some Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^m$. Consider maps $u : B^n \to N$ in the Sobolev space
$$W^{1,n}(B^n, N) := \{ u \in W^{1,n}(B^n, \mathbb{R}^m) : u(x) \in N \text{ for a.e. } x \in B^n \}.$$
The $n$-Dirichlet energy is defined by
$$E_n(u) := \int_{B^n} |\nabla u(x)|^n \, dx.$$
A map $u \in W^{1,n}(B^n, N)$ is called weakly $n$-harmonic if it is a critical point of $E_n$ with respect to range variations, i.e., for every smooth vector field $X$ on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that is tangent to $N$ along $N$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0} E_n(\pi_N(u + tX \circ u)) = 0,$$
where $\pi_N$ denotes nearest-point projection onto $N$ (defined in a tubular neighborhood). Equivalently, $u$ satisfies the Euler–Lagrange system
$$-\operatorname{div}(|\nabla u|^{n-2} \nabla u) \perp T_u N \quad \text{in } \mathcal{D}'(B^n).$$

Question: Must every weakly $n$-harmonic map $u \in W^{1,n}(B^n, N)$ be continuous on $B^n$?
artifact.status_search_result: The continuity (regularity) of arbitrary weakly $n$-harmonic maps in $W^{1,n}(B^n,N)$ in the critical-exponent case $p=n$ for general closed target manifolds $N$ is still listed as an open problem. Continuity is known in special cases (e.g., target a sphere, or under smallness in a Morrey norm, or for stationary/minimizing maps), but the general case remains unresolved as of recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Regularity of p-harmonic maps from the p-dimensional ball into a sphere
status_evidence.snippet: For p ≥ 2, all weakly p-harmonic maps from the p-dimensional ball into a sphere are Hölder continuous.
status_evidence.claim: Continuity of weakly n-harmonic maps is known when the target is a sphere, but not in general.

status_evidence.title: A Note on Moving Frames along Sobolev Maps and the Regularity of Weakly Harmonic Maps
status_evidence.snippet: Regularity results for weakly harmonic maps under smallness assumptions on the gradient in Morrey norm.
status_evidence.claim: General continuity for weakly n-harmonic maps into arbitrary closed targets remains open; only conditional results are available.
